name: Rhode Island

private_challenge.form_or_statute: R.I. Gen. Laws 17-9.1-28: affidavit prescribed by the State Board of Elections, filed with the local board of canvassers; certified-mail notice and a hearing where the voter answers under oath (citizenship questions in (c)(1)). 410-RICR-20-00-20: a separate affidavit for each challenged voter, with supporting documents attached.
private_challenge.deadlines: All information and documents must be filed at least 20 days before the election; no supplements after that. No one may be removed within 90 days before an election except on request, sworn statement of moving, conviction, incapacity, or death (410-RICR-20-00-20).
private_challenge.evidence_standard: Affidavit based on the affiant's personal knowledge, setting forth evidence that creates 'a reasonable cause to suspect' the voter is not eligible (17-9.1-28(a); 410-RICR-20-00-20).
private_challenge.false_statement_penalty: Willful and malicious challenge without reasonable cause: misdemeanor, plus liability for compensatory and punitive damages and counsel fees (17-9.1-29).

sources.cite: 410-RICR-20-00-20 (challenge regulation: one affidavit per voter, personal knowledge, 20-day filing rule, 90-day removal limit)
R.I. Gen. Laws 17-9.1-29 (penalty for unsubstantiated challenge)
R.I. Gen. Laws 17-9.1-30 (appeal to the State Board of Elections)

state_windows.effect: No removal within 90 days before an election except on the voter's request or listed grounds (not citizenship).
All affidavits and documents must be filed at least 20 days before the election.

county_board.name: Rhode Island local boards of canvassers (Board of Elections)
county_board.note: Challenges under 17-9.1-28 go to the local board of canvassers.

gates.basis: Jury records: status unknown (null), so counts only. Rhode Island allows a private challenge on personal knowledge and reasonable cause, filed 20 days ahead (17-9.1-28). Guidance stays off while the jury list is not available.

notes: A malicious challenge without reasonable cause is a misdemeanor and exposes the challenger to punitive damages (17-9.1-29).
The challenge rule requires personal knowledge (410-RICR-20-00-20). A data match alone is unlikely to qualify.
